sources.title: Grass-roots of Adaptation: Strengthening community climate resilience through locally led adaptation in Costa Rica
sources.organization: Fundecooperación para el Desarrollo Sostenible; submitted to the Adaptation Fund
sources.temporal_coverage: Proposal contextualizes historical meteorological records from 1980–2017 and regional adaptation risks; proposal version July 2025.
sources.methodology: Proposal summarizes IMN hazard records and regional risks.
sources.limitations: Applicant proposal; regional summaries rely on prior government analyses and do not attribute events.

sources.title: United Nations organizations’ support to community-driven recovery, risk knowledge and governance enhances disaster and climate resilience in Costa Rica
sources.organization: United Nations Office for Disaster Risk Reduction (UNDRR)
sources.temporal_coverage: Reports 2017 Storm Nate recovery and United Nations-supported risk and resilience work through 2023.
sources.methodology: UNDRR summarizes program activities and risk findings.
sources.limitations: Program account; no independent impact evaluation.

sources.title: Informe de progreso del Plan Nacional de Adaptación al Cambio Climático de Costa Rica 2022-2026
sources.organization: Dirección de Cambio Climático, Ministerio de Ambiente y Energía; GIZ and IISD
sources.temporal_coverage: Implementation progress of the 2022–2026 National Adaptation Plan, assessed through June 2026.
sources.methodology: Questionnaires, consultation and document review assessed NAP products through June 2026.
sources.limitations: Progress covered 179 of 232 products; institutional self-report is not impact evaluation.

sources.title: Proyectos Climáticos
sources.organization: Dirección de Cambio Climático, Ministerio de Ambiente y Energía (MINAE)
sources.temporal_coverage: MINAE project-register entries with stated project durations; the page does not provide publication or project-status dates for every entry.
sources.methodology: Official registry lists project aims, locations and durations.
sources.limitations: Entries describe design; status and outcomes are unreported.

claims.paraphrase: In 1980–2017, events were most frequent in Limón, Puntarenas and Alajuela; 72% were heavy rain, storms or hail.
claims.limitations: Historical hazard series; not attribution to climate change.

claims.locator: PDF p. 9, Chorotega Region risk summary
claims.paraphrase: Chorotega droughts primarily affect agriculture; extreme rain mainly impacts roads, farms and homes.

claims.locator: PDF p. 10, Huetar Caribe Region risk summary
claims.paraphrase: Huetar Caribe extreme rainfall mainly affects roads, farms, rivers and streams; cited risks also include farm and fishing yields.
claims.limitations: The region-wide summary does not disaggregate household impacts.

claims.locator: PDF p. 12, Brunca Region context and risk summary
claims.paraphrase: Brunca has 12 Indigenous territories and the country’s largest Indigenous population; risks include agricultural and service disruption.
claims.scenario: Potential regional climate risks are identified; the cited passage specifies no emissions pathway or projection period.
claims.limitations: Potential risk summary without a stated climate scenario or quantified exposure.

claims.locator: PDF p. 13, ‘Communities and Vulnerable Groups in Adaptation’
claims.paraphrase: Listed vulnerable groups include rural/coastal women in informal work and Indigenous communities lacking resources, water, electricity or internet.
claims.limitations: Proposal summarizes NDC/NAP findings; not a new household survey.

claims.locator: HTML lines 8–10, national hazard and vulnerability context
claims.paraphrase: UNDRR reports heavy rain and drought in Costa Rica in 2023 and lists floods, hurricanes, storms, drought and water scarcity as climate-exacerbated hazards.
claims.limitations: National risk statement; not local attribution.

claims.locator: HTML lines 11–12, Acosta after Storm Nate
claims.paraphrase: After October 2017 Storm Nate, about 20,000 Acosta residents were cut off for days without water, electricity, food or medicine.
claims.limitations: Historical case; no climate attribution stated.

claims.locator: HTML lines 12–16, Acosta recovery and local-government network
claims.paraphrase: Acosta residents organized food/medicine delivery and recovery planning; over 400 participated, helping inspire 32 municipalities to join an SDG network.
claims.limitations: UNDRR reports participation and network membership, not measured recovery outcomes.

claims.paraphrase: Over 15,000 volunteer water managers serve nearly 30% of residents; support reinforced pipes, hydrants, weather stations and watershed warnings.
institutions: Instituto Costarricense de Acueductos y Alcantarillados (AyA)
claims.limitations: UNDRR account reports program reach and activities, not representative performance or outcome evaluation.

claims.locator: HTML lines 22–25, systemic infrastructure risk assessment
claims.paraphrase: A 2023 assessment found about 60% of critical roads and bridges vulnerable to floods.
institutions: National Commission for Risk Prevention and Emergency Response (CNE)
claims.limitations: Article summarizes the assessment but does not provide location-level results.

claims.paraphrase: By June 2026, 67 of 232 NAP products were complete, 66 in progress, 43 unstarted or canceled, and 56 lacked progress information.
claims.limitations: The review obtained information on 179 products; 56 had no progress data.

claims.locator: PDF p. 19, implementation by financing source
claims.paraphrase: Of 144 products conditioned on external finance, 44 were complete, 37 progressing, 32 canceled or unstarted and 31 unknown; some needed funds did not materialize.
claims.limitations: Counts describe implementation status, not adaptation impact.

claims.locator: PDF p. 32, water-security products for Central and Huetar Norte
claims.paraphrase: A planned automated groundwater network for Central and Huetar Norte was to track water levels, temperature and conductivity, but its progress was unreported.
institutions: Instituto Costarricense de Acueductos y Alcantarillados (AyA)
claims.limitations: NAP progress report lists this product without implementation information.

claims.locator: HTML lines 5–6, Indigenous family-agriculture project entry
claims.paraphrase: A 36-month project targets resilient family farming and food security with Bribri and Cabécar organizations in Talamanca’s Valle de la Estrella.
claims.limitations: Registry describes project aims and duration, not delivery or outcomes.

claims.locator: HTML lines 26–27, Nicoya-area water adaptation project entry
claims.paraphrase: A Nicoya-area project aims to reduce water-use conflict and prevent future disputes as water deficit increases.
claims.scenario: Project register states an intended future-conflict prevention pathway; it does not provide a climate scenario or measured results.
institutions: Municipalities of Nicoya, Hojancha and Nandayure
claims.limitations: This is a project objective, not evidence that conflict occurred or was prevented.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: It links increasing water deficit to future water-use conflict; HTML lines 26–27.

claims.locator: HTML lines 52–53, Huetar Norte smallholder project entry
claims.paraphrase: A Huetar Norte program lists 36-month adaptation support on 60 farms for soil/water conservation, crop diversity and water harvesting.
claims.limitations: Registry states program design, not implementation or measured resilience.

claims.locator: HTML line 23, Paquera-Tambor marine-fisheries project entry
claims.paraphrase: A Paquera-Tambor project proposes coastal-ecosystem protection and climate-adaptation capacity-building with fisher associations.
institutions: Paquera-Tambor Marine Responsible Fishing Area Commission
claims.limitations: Registry lists intended measures and a 15-month duration without reported outcomes.

search_audit.query: Costa Rica official regional climate vulnerability report Chorotega Huetar Caribe Brunca Indigenous territories adaptation
search_audit.outcome: Inspected a public Adaptation Fund proposal with region-specific risk summaries, the UNDRR Acosta case and the 2026 NAP progress report; named regions and groups were available, while several assessments remain region-level.

search_audit.query: Costa Rica climate water deficit conflicts over use Nicoya official adaptation project
search_audit.outcome: MINAE project register explicitly states a proposed pathway from increasing water deficit to potential future water-use conflicts and capacity-building to reduce them; this is a project objective, not an observed causal finding. IACHR land-violence evidence was reviewed separately and not linked to climate.

search_audit.query: Costa Rica violence organized crime land conflict obstructing climate adaptation or disaster response report
search_audit.outcome: IACHR reports Indigenous land disputes and violence, while inspected climate/disaster reports document adaptation and response; no source inspected states that violence or insecurity interrupted these climate actions, so no reverse link is asserted.

search_audit.query: Costa Rica community disaster resilience Acosta rural water associations local adaptation capacity report
search_audit.outcome: UNDRR documents Acosta recovery, volunteer ASADA water management and systemic-risk assessment; MINAE records local adaptation projects and the NAP progress review reports product-level implementation and funding status.

gaps: CRI has no baseline dossier in EXISTING_COUNTRIES.json or countries/CRI in this worktree; this is a new-country extraction.

The only explicit climate-to-conflict pathway located is a MINAE project objective concerning water-use conflict and rising water deficit near Nicoya; the register does not establish observed conflict or project effectiveness.
The IACHR reports Indigenous land occupation and violence, but the inspected chapter does not connect those events to climate hazards or adaptation; no such link is inferred.
No inspected primary source states that violence or insecurity interrupted climate adaptation or disaster response in Costa Rica.

Regional event records summarized in the Adaptation Fund proposal end in 2017 and are not a current, climate-attributed exposure inventory; several regional risk statements lack scenario and household-level estimates.
The 2026 NAP progress review covered 179 of 232 products; 56 had no progress information and 43 were unstarted or canceled, limiting assessment of implementation outcomes.
